reviewedBy: Codex manual review of explicit synthetic scenarios; no independent human-label claim
labelingPolicy: One case / target detector is one scoring unit. Pattern labels describe recorded recurrence, size, compaction or parse gaps. Candidate labels mean eligible for a bounded investigation/trial, not proven waste or savings. Explicit verification, post-edit checks and user annotations are review-only. Missing capture capability is unscored. Other detectors are outside each case's target label.

cases.rationale: Three unchanged complete reads of the same target and text; no recorded verification intent.
Two observations do not establish the defined three-read recurrence.
Read text changes; exact-content recurrence is absent.
Repeated text exists but the task explicitly requires independent verification.
Recorded edit precedes the reads; required post-change checks remain review-only.
Captured fragments repeat, but complete source equality is not established.
Missing keyed equality capability; do not score unknown as a true negative.
Three comparable failed commands in one ten-minute window, with no recorded progress.
Only two comparable failures.
Explicit retry/verification protocol makes this necessary repetition.
Comparable command subsequently succeeds; preserved evidence is review-only, not ongoing failed work.
Edits between attempts establish changed diagnostic steps rather than one unchanged episode.
Repeated observations of the same process handle are polling, not new failed attempts.
Complete captured output meets the declared 256-KiB size boundary; reduction still needs a trial.
Complete output is below the published size definition.
User annotation declares this complete evidence necessary; do not offer an optimization candidate.
Three distinct completed operation IDs within five minutes.
Repeated lifecycle notifications share one operation ID; they are one operation.
Started operations without completion do not establish a completed burst.
Distinct operations are spaced six minutes apart, outside one burst window.
A terminated malformed JSONL record creates a retained parse gap.
A valid future envelope is unsupported, not a malformed-record gap.
An unterminated partial record remains pending, not a completed parse gap.
Gap evidence remains, but resolved user feedback makes the plan review-only.
